newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan puts off telecom privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan puts off telecom privatisation.

text.p: Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government has put off the planned privatisation of Pakistan's large state telecommunication sector until it can get a better price, a government minister said on Friday.
Communications Minister Azam Khan Hoti made the announcement in a speech at Haripur in the North West Frontier province.

"I had the privatisation process postponed as there were lots of liabilities on the PTCL (Pakistan Telecommunications Company Limited), TIP (Telephone Industries of Pakistan) and other government-owned telecommunication organisations," he said in an address to TIP workers.
He said though the telecommunication sector was making a profit, it had over the years incurred a lot of liabilities, which needed to be settled before privatisation.

"Once all the liabilities are settled, the telecommunication sector will yield a very good price," Hoti said."We want to show profits both in the ledger and the accounts to make some real difference."
Pakistan's plans to sell a 26 percent stake in PTCL and transfer management control to a strategic investor have suffered repeated delays since the original target date of December 1995.

Last year, then prime minister Benazir Bhutto's government said it was delaying the PTCL privasation for some time because it feared it would not get a good price while telecom privatisation was going on in many other countries.
However, in December, a caretaker government that was in office said it had put the PTCL at the top of its privatisation agenda and expected the sale to take place in a few months.
Hoti did not say when he expected the telecom sector to be ready for privatisation.
